title: Choose CampusKart's visual world
question: The roll assigned the UPI Receipt world. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: UPI Receipt
options.lineage: GPay / PhonePe payment-success screens every student opens daily
options.thesis: Every database transaction lands like a UPI payment: a tick, a big amount, a reference and what changed.
options.viewport: Indigo shell with search and Sell; AI picks grid with reasons and a match meter; right rail shows the last transaction as a receipt plus live activity rows.
options.risk: Can read as a fintech app if listings stay timid; the receipt must stay a moment, never wallpaper.

raised.raise: Live rows: offers, orders and the audit log restyle in place (amber pending, red cancelled) inside fixed columns.
One fixed strength meter for AI match, shared viewers and spam score, used identically everywhere.
Coral is reserved for the next action (Sell, Make offer, Accept) and nothing else.
Everything snaps to one 8px cell; rupee figures are tabular and right-aligned.
Every panel has a budget: a fixed number of rows, then a total line and View all.

options.label: Campus Notice Board
options.lineage: department corridor cork boards with pinned FOR SALE slips
options.thesis: Listings are the slips students already pin up; the tear-off phone strip becomes the order.
options.viewport: Cork-brown header; listings as straight paper slips with a pin and a tear-off price strip; activity card stamped with trigger outcomes.
options.risk: The most familiar campus metaphor, where most runs land; at worst a skeuomorphic cork-board cliché, and slips must stay straight to stay scannable.

options.label: Reels-style Discover
options.lineage: full-screen vertical feeds students scroll every night
options.thesis: On phones, browsing becomes one listing per screen with Save, Offer and Buy on a right rail.
options.viewport: Phone: one listing fills the screen, price and AI reason anchored low, action rail on the right.
options.case: Students identify with it instantly; it loses on clarity because a feed hides price comparison and the admin side gains nothing.
options.risk: Hands the app a navigation model the working-screen rules reserve for standard patterns.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: Listings and offers as rows on a live departure board.
options.viewport: A board of rows; shopping images have nowhere to live.
options.case: Strong for the audit log, weak for browsing items with pictures.
options.risk: Turns a shop into a timetable.
options.kept: Live rows that restyle in place without breaking the grid.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Listings as stars, also-viewed links as constellations.
options.viewport: A sky of listings; prices hard to compare.
options.case: Students do not shop by star chart; clarity and identification both lose.
options.kept: One fixed magnitude ramp for every strength value.

options.label: Terminal Yellow Wayfinding
options.thesis: Each screen signs only the next decision.
options.viewport: Yellow bands over content, one decision at a time.
options.case: Few students live in airports; yellow everywhere fights product art.
options.kept: One colour reserved for the next action only.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Prices built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.viewport: A poster grid more than a shop.
options.case: Design-school reference, not a student one; clarity drops.
options.risk: Reads as a poster, not a product.
options.kept: A strict cell grid that everything snaps to.

options.label: Cassette J-card
options.thesis: Buying and selling as side A and side B.
options.viewport: A folded inlay; too small for a catalogue.
options.case: A generation too early for this audience; clarity also loses.
options.kept: Fixed budgets per panel, closed by a total line.

canonCard.label: Marketplace standard
canonCard.thesis: What OLX, Amazon and Vinted ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Top search, category strip, five-across product grid.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every marketplace by design.
